name: Hexagonal architecture (ports and adapters)
essence: The application core talks to the outside world only through ports, which are purposeful conversations; adapters plug technologies into ports. The application can be driven equally by users, programs, tests or batch jobs, and developed and tested in isolation from databases and UIs. The hexagon is only a drawing convention: it leaves room to add as many ports and adapters as needed, where a layered drawing forces a one-dimensional picture.
best_when: The default choice for most projects: infrastructure-independent, swappable components, and in-memory adapters that make tests trivial.

name: Clean and onion architecture
essence: The same dependency rule as hexagonal, expressed as concentric layers that point inward.
best_when: The same family as hexagonal; pick the vocabulary your team already has.
origin_author: Robert C. Martin and Jeffrey Palermo

name: Functional core, imperative shell
essence: Pure decision logic in the core; I/O and effects in a thin shell.
best_when: Pairs naturally with hexagonal and with type-driven design.

name: Domain-driven design
essence: Model the business language: bounded contexts, aggregates, value objects and a ubiquitous language.
best_when: Complex domains; it supplies the inside of the hexagon.

name: Vertical slices
essence: Organise code by feature or use case rather than by technical layer.
best_when: Change locality; CRUD-heavy or API-driven applications.

name: Modular monolith
essence: Real modules with enforced boundaries, deployed as one unit.
best_when: Most teams: it avoids the operating cost of microservices and keeps the option to extract services later.

name: CQRS and event sourcing
essence: Separate read and write models; keep state as a log of events.
best_when: Only where audit, temporal or scale needs justify the cost.

name: Evolutionary architecture with fitness functions
essence: Automated checks, such as dependency-rule tests and complexity or coupling budgets, keep the architecture honest.
best_when: Always: boundaries without enforcement rot into a big ball of mud.
